# 2 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** One finds also in the records that Jeremiah the prophet ordered those who were being deported to take some of the fire, as we have mentioned,

**2** and that the prophet, after giving them the law, instructed those who were being deported not to forget the commandments of the LORD, and not to be led astray in their thoughts when they saw the gold and silver idols and their ornamentation.

**3** And with other such exhortations he urged them that the law should not be removed from their hearts.

**4** The same writing also says that, moved by a divine oracle, the prophet gave orders that the tent of meeting and the ark should accompany him, as he went out to the mountain where Moses had climbed and had seen the inheritance of God.

**5** When Jeremiah arrived, he found a cave there. He brought in the tent, the ark, and the altar of incense, and then he sealed the entrance.

**6** Some of those who had followed tried to mark the way so they could find it again, but they were unable to.

**7** When Jeremiah heard of this, he rebuked them and declared: "The place shall remain unknown until God gathers his people together again and shows his mercy.

**8** Then the LORD will reveal these things, and the glory of the LORD will appear, together with the cloud, as they appeared to Moses and as Solomon asked that the place might be greatly hallowed."

**9** It was also made clear that he, possessing wisdom, offered a sacrifice at the dedication and completion of the temple.

**10** Just as Moses prayed to the LORD and fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifices, so also Solomon prayed and fire came down and consumed the whole burnt offerings.

**11** And Moses said, "Because the sin offering was not eaten, it was consumed in the fire."

**12** In the same way Solomon kept the eight days of dedication.

**13** These same things are also reported in the records and in the memoirs of Nehemiah: how he founded a library and gathered together the writings about the kings and the prophets, and the writings of David, and letters of kings concerning votive offerings.

**14** In the same way Judas collected all the writings that had been scattered because of the war that had come upon us, and these writings are now in our possession.

**15** If you have need of them, send messengers to obtain them.

**16** Since, then, we are about to celebrate the purification, we write to you. You will do well, therefore, to observe these days.

**17** It is God who has saved all his people and has given to all the inheritance and the kingship and the priesthood and the consecration,

**18** as he promised through the law. We trust in God that he will soon have mercy on us and gather us from everywhere under heaven to the holy place; for he has rescued us from great evils and has purified the place.

**19** This is the account of Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, and of the purification of the great temple, and of the dedication of the altar,

**20** and further of the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,

**21** and of the appearances that came from heaven to those who fought zealously for Judaism, so that, few as they were, they plundered the whole land and drove away the barbarian hordes,

**22** recovered the temple renowned throughout the whole world, freed the city, and restored the laws that were in danger of being abolished — and all this because the LORD in his great clemency became gracious toward them.

**23** All these things, which were set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five volumes, we shall attempt to condense into a single book.

**24** For considering the flood of statistics and the difficulty facing those who wish to enter into the narratives of history because of the mass of the material,

**25** we have aimed to please those who wish to read, to make it easy for those who wish to memorize, and to be useful to all who take up the book.

**26** For us who have undertaken the labor of abbreviation, the task is not easy but requires effort and long watching,

**27** just as it is no light matter for one who prepares a feast and seeks the benefit of others. In order to win the gratitude of many, however, we will gladly accept this thankless labor.

**28** Leaving the precise details of every event to the historian, we will apply ourselves to following the rules of a summary account.

**29** For as the master builder of a new house must be concerned with the whole structure, while the one who undertakes the encaustic painting is concerned only with what is appropriate for decoration — so too is it with us.

**30** To examine every detail and to range over the whole subject belongs to the one who undertakes an original history;

**31** but the one who makes an epitome should be permitted to aim at conciseness of expression and to renounce the full treatment of the matter.

**32** Let us begin the narrative here, with no more preamble — for it would be foolish to write at length in the introduction and then to abridge the history itself.
